sources.name: lexiforest/curl-impersonate
sources.claimedVersionsNote: Active fork of curl-impersonate. Ships browser profile binaries/presets (chromeNNN, firefoxNNN, safari*). Exact majors move with releases; use upstream fingerprint docs / `curl-cffi list` rather than assuming a fixed set. Preferred low-cost capture path for tool-matched goldens.
sources.notes: Do not copy JA3 strings from issues/blogs into goldens. Capture ClientHello via tool self-connect to a local probe, then fill entries/* only after measurement.

sources.name: lexiforest/curl_cffi
sources.claimedVersionsNote: Python binding to the lexiforest curl-impersonate fork. Supports impersonate=chromeNNN / safari* / firefox* presets; skipped majors mean 'reuse previous TLS fingerprint with updated headers'. CLI: `curl-cffi` (list/update since ~v0.15). Low-cost path on Windows without full browser installers.
sources.notes: Tool JA3 may differ slightly from real Chrome; tool-matched only.

sources.name: lwthiker/curl-impersonate
sources.claimedVersionsNote: Original project (last major release series ~0.6.x). Historical profiles around Chrome ~116 and Firefox ~117 era in browsers.json; still useful as a reference CLI shape and older goldens, but prefer lexiforest fork for current majors.
sources.notes: Inventory only — do not treat archived majors as current browser-matched.

sources.name: refraction-networking/utls
sources.claimedVersionsNote: Go library with HelloChrome_NNN / HelloFirefox_NNN / HelloIOS_* ClientHello IDs (e.g. Chrome 120/131/133-class parrots in recent tags). Fingerprints live in u_parrots.go — library-level, not a browser capture.
sources.notes: Useful for cross-checking extension/cipher ordering notes. Capture still requires emitting a real ClientHello against a probe.

sources.name: wreq / rquest-class Rust stacks
sources.claimedVersionsNote: Rust HTTP clients built around BoringSSL/impersonate-style profiles (Chrome/Safari/Firefox majors vary by crate version). Relevant long-horizon for ShowNet MITM stack research; not wired as product engine today.
sources.notes: Inventory for implementers evaluating Phase-1 impersonate connectors. Shipping product still rustls-only with ja3Parity=false.

sources.name: FoxIO-LLC/ja4
sources.claimedVersionsNote: Authoritative JA4+ specification and reference implementations (not a browser impersonate client). Use for algorithm/canonical-string verification when recomputing ja4/ja4Raw from captured ClientHello. Does not ship Chrome major presets for outbound MITM.
sources.notes: Spec/reference only. Never paste example JA4 strings from docs into goldens as if they were measured captures.

sources.name: salesforce/ja3
sources.claimedVersionsNote: Original JA3 standard (archived May 2025). Historical algorithm reference; FoxIO JA4 supersedes for new work. No current Chrome major matrix.
sources.notes: Archived. Use only for JA3 canonical algorithm cross-check, never as a golden source.

sources.name: Danny-Dasilva/CycleTLS
sources.claimedVersionsNote: Go/JS library that spoofs TLS JA3 fingerprints with configurable ClientHello. Useful as an alternate tool-capture path for custom ja3 strings; version coverage depends on user-supplied fingerprints, not a fixed browser matrix.
sources.notes: tool-matched only when ClientHello is actually captured against a probe; do not treat configured JA3 strings alone as goldens.
